questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the meaning of the following terms:

(i) Infectious disease

(ii) Epidemic disease

(iii) Incubation period. *(2, 2, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **infectious disease** is a disease caused by a **pathogen** (a bacterium, virus, fungus, protozoan or other parasite) that can be **passed** from an infected person (or animal) to another person.

(ii) An **epidemic disease** is a disease that **spreads quickly** and affects **many people** in a community or region at the same time (for example cholera or meningitis).

(iii) The **incubation period** is the **time** between the **entry** of the pathogen into the body and the **appearance of the first symptoms** of the disease.

questions.enonce_markdown: How are contagious diseases spread? *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A contagious disease is an infectious disease that spreads from one person to another by contact. It is spread by:

1. **Direct contact** with an infected person: touching, skin contact or **sexual contact** (scabies, ringworm, gonorrhoea, syphilis, HIV/AIDS).
2. **Droplets** from the **coughing, sneezing** or speaking of an infected person, which are breathed in by others (common cold, influenza, tuberculosis, measles).
3. **Contaminated food and water**, for example food touched by dirty hands or visited by flies, or water polluted by faeces (cholera, typhoid, dysentery).
4. **Contaminated objects** (towels, clothes, combs, bedding, razor blades, handkerchiefs) used by an infected person (ringworm, scabies, eye infections).
5. **Blood contact**: contaminated needles and syringes, blood transfusion, or open wounds (HIV/AIDS, hepatitis B).
6. **From mother to child**: across the placenta, during birth or in breast milk (HIV/AIDS, syphilis).
7. **Vectors** (living carriers such as mosquitoes and houseflies) that carry the germs from one person to another (malaria, yellow fever, diarrhoea).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using the following headings describe the disease cholera:

(i) Causative agent

(ii) A mode of transmission

(iii) Two symptoms

(iv) Two control measures. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Causative agent:** the bacterium ***Vibrio cholerae***.

**(ii) A mode of transmission:** by drinking **water** or eating **food contaminated with the faeces** of an infected person, for example food carried or touched by **houseflies** or by unwashed hands.

**(iii) Two symptoms:** (1) severe **watery diarrhoea** ("rice-water" stools); (2) **vomiting**, which together cause **dehydration**, muscular cramps and weakness.

**(iv) Two control measures:** (1) provide **clean, treated or boiled drinking water** and protect water sources from contamination; (2) proper **disposal of sewage and refuse**, use of latrines, **washing the hands** with soap after using the toilet and before eating, and covering food and controlling flies. (Also: vaccination, isolation of patients, and **oral rehydration therapy** for treatment.)
